title: Zero Trust MVP · Customer journey
subtitle: From a research method and synthetic source data to a reviewed, accepted sample output.

persona.name: Researcher / method author
persona.goal: Use a reviewed research method on an appropriate source, understand each handoff, and obtain an accepted result with traceable context.
persona.trigger: A researcher has a method to introduce and a dataset to process.
persona.endState: The method is published after four reviews; a completed demo run has a separately accepted output and its synthetic sample can be downloaded.

evidenceNote: This is a source-backed journey of the implemented MVP, illustrated with fresh UI screenshots. Customer questions, pains and gains are hypotheses inferred from the workflow, not findings from interviews or measured customer outcomes.

configuration.label: Feature selection
configuration.value: All included MVP capabilities are always on. There is no MVP feature-toggle setup.

configuration.label: Roles selected
configuration.value: Researcher → Ethical reviewer → Technical reviewer → Privacy reviewer → Security reviewer → Researcher → Privacy reviewer for output → Researcher.

configuration.label: Review policy
configuration.value: Every submitted pipeline/version requires all four separate reviews, followed by a separate Researcher publication.

configuration.label: Scenario
configuration.value: New Customer journey outcome classifier v1.0.0, synthetic CSV cohort, and one optional synthetic text-evidence attachment.

configuration.label: Simulation controls
configuration.value: Available for solo demos; not used for the captured main journey. Reviewer decisions and publication were exercised through their normal UI controls.

boundaries: The prototype uses local browser state and demo role switching. It does not provide real authentication, enforced access control or organizational approval routing.
Dataset imports save metadata and column names. File contents are not uploaded; temporary import preview rows are discarded when the import dialog closes. Attached text evidence is retained locally.
The repository URL is recorded without fetching or analyzing code. Review checklists are human demonstration confirmations, not scanner findings.
Execution is simulated and output rows are synthetic fixtures. Format matching does not verify schema mapping. The CSV download contains the small synthetic sample, not a full processed dataset.
Activity and support records are local demonstrations, not an immutable audit service or external help desk. CSV downloads themselves are not recorded as activity events.

stages.title: Prepare the source data
stages.goal: Start with an identifiable, inspectable source.
stages.customerQuestion: Can I explore this without uploading real research data?
stages.customerAction: Open Datasets, choose Import dataset, use the synthetic example, inspect columns and sample rows, then import.
stages.teamAction: The browser validates the CSV shape and registers metadata and column names locally.
stages.handoff: Researcher retains ownership; the registered source can be selected later in Configure run.
stages.successSignal: The synthetic cohort appears in Datasets after import.
stages.painHypothesis: Unclear source identity or format could lead to choosing the wrong data.
stages.gainHypothesis: Preview and explicit metadata make the chosen source easier to recognize.
stages.caption: The import dialog shows the synthetic CSV, preview rows, dataset name and Import dataset action. The starting pipeline catalog is included as supporting context.
stages.limit: CSV shape validation is demonstrated; no dataset upload or enforced permission check occurs.

stages.title: Describe and submit the method
stages.goal: Give reviewers enough purpose, source and contract context.
stages.customerQuestion: What do reviewers need, and who owns the next step?
stages.customerAction: Complete the three-step pipeline wizard, attach optional synthetic evidence, inspect the final summary and submit for review. Save a named draft when not ready.
stages.teamAction: Submission records the method/version and starts Ethical review. The author receives a status receipt and next owner.
stages.handoff: Researcher → Ethical reviewer. The author cannot approve the pending stage.
stages.successSignal: The receipt says Submitted for review and identifies the Ethical reviewer as next owner.
stages.painHypothesis: Scattered requirements and unclear handoffs could cause repeated follow-up.
stages.gainHypothesis: A structured submission and clear receipt provide a shared starting point.
stages.caption: The final wizard summary exposes the research purpose, source, version, contracts and attached evidence before submission. The receipt shows the subsequent reviewer handoff.
stages.limit: The repository URL is descriptive metadata; the prototype does not fetch research code.

stages.title: Complete organizational review
stages.customerQuestion: Which review is pending, and what would unblock it?
stages.customerAction: Track the submission and next owner. If a reviewer requests changes or rejects it, read the reason, revise and resubmit.
stages.teamAction: Ethical, Technical, Privacy and Security reviewers each inspect their own evidence, confirm three criteria and make a distinct decision, in that order.
stages.handoff: Ethical → Technical → Privacy → Security → Researcher. In the demo, switch roles to act as each participant.
stages.successSignal: After Security approval the status is Ready to publish; the method is still not published.
stages.painHypothesis: An opaque queue or one generic approval could hide accountability and missing review stages.
stages.gainHypothesis: Separate stage criteria, named owners and decision history make each handoff explicit.
stages.caption: Four distinct reviewer screens show their stage-specific checklists. The captured run checked each criterion and used the normal approval action; it did not simulate approval.
stages.limit: Reviewers confirm illustrative evidence. No automated ethics, runtime, privacy or security assessment is claimed.

stages.title: Publish the reviewed version
stages.goal: Decide when the reviewed method becomes available to run.
stages.customerQuestion: Are all reviews complete, and is this the version I want to release?
stages.customerAction: Return to Researcher and choose Publish pipeline after all four reviews are complete.
stages.teamAction: Publication records its own event and changes the pipeline to Approved.
stages.handoff: Review team → Researcher; publication is a separate author decision.
stages.successSignal: Pipeline details say Ready for research and offer Configure run and New version.
stages.painHypothesis: Review completion could be mistaken for release, making availability unclear.
stages.gainHypothesis: Explicit author publication separates assessment from making a version runnable.
stages.caption: The published pipeline is ready for research. The supporting screen shows the previous Ready to publish state with a distinct Publish pipeline action.
stages.limit: Publication changes local prototype state; it does not deploy research code.

stages.title: Run the approved method
stages.goal: Pair the published version with a compatible source and follow execution.
stages.customerQuestion: Does the source fit this method, and has the run actually finished?
stages.customerAction: Configure a run with the approved pipeline and imported cohort. Inspect the declared input and dataset columns, start the demo, then open run details.
stages.teamAction: A local timer advances four labelled execution steps and produces a synthetic artifact marked Pending review.
stages.handoff: Researcher → simulated execution → Privacy reviewer for the output decision.
stages.successSignal: Run status is Completed and Inspect output opens an artifact awaiting privacy validation.
stages.painHypothesis: A format mismatch or an unexplained run state could make recovery difficult.
stages.gainHypothesis: Visible contracts and separate run/output statuses clarify what is complete and what remains.
stages.caption: Completed run details retain method, dataset and version context and link to the output. The supporting Configure run screen shows the chosen pipeline, dataset and columns.
stages.limit: The prototype checks format only, not schema mapping. No research code runs on a backend.

stages.title: Validate the generated output
stages.goal: Assess this particular output before it becomes downloadable.
stages.customerQuestion: Does approving the method also mean its output is acceptable?
stages.customerAction: Inspect the synthetic output preview and provenance. In the demo, use Switch role to perform the output handoff.
stages.teamAction: The Privacy reviewer deliberately chooses Acceptable or Not acceptable and submits the decision. Rejection requires an explanation.
stages.handoff: Researcher → Privacy reviewer → Researcher after acceptance. This is separate from the pipeline Privacy review.
stages.successSignal: Acceptance changes the artifact to Validated; a rejection keeps download blocked.
stages.painHypothesis: A generated output could be mistaken for an already validated one.
stages.gainHypothesis: A distinct output decision and receipt make download eligibility understandable.
stages.caption: The output review shows synthetic rows, provenance, a deliberately selected Acceptable option, validation comments and Accept output. The capture also verified download was blocked before acceptance.
stages.limit: The output preview is a fixture for demonstration, not a PHI scan or a computation over imported source records.

stages.title: Retrieve the accepted sample
stages.customerQuestion: What am I downloading, and why is it available now?
stages.customerAction: Return to Researcher, reopen the accepted output, read the validation receipt and choose Download sample CSV.
stages.teamAction: The browser downloads the small synthetic preview fixture; the artifact remains Validated.
stages.handoff: The researcher obtains a local file and keeps the run/version/decision context in the prototype.
stages.successSignal: The Download sample CSV action is enabled and the browser emits a CSV download.
stages.painHypothesis: Unclear output labels could imply a full processed result when only a sample exists.
stages.gainHypothesis: The sample label and acceptance receipt set the right expectation for this prototype.
stages.caption: The researcher sees Output accepted and the enabled sample-download action. A supporting phone capture shows the same accepted artifact with full-width mobile CTAs. The capture run exercised and checked the CSV download.
stages.limit: The downloaded file is a synthetic sample, not the declared full-record-count output.

stages.title: Trace decisions and improve the method
stages.goal: Understand the recorded decisions and choose the next iteration.
stages.customerQuestion: Which version and decisions led to this output, and how do I continue?
stages.customerAction: Open Activity log, search/filter the relevant work, export its history or reopen an entity. To improve the method, open the published pipeline and choose New version.
stages.teamAction: History shows recorded actors, versions, review decisions, publication and execution/output events. A new version starts all four reviews again while the earlier approved version stays runnable.
stages.handoff: Any participant can inspect history. A new-version journey returns ownership to the researcher and then the review team.
stages.successSignal: Filtered history exports as JSON; related entities reopen their current state. Iteration is available from the approved version.
stages.painHypothesis: Context scattered across versions and handoffs could make it hard to explain how an output was reached.
stages.gainHypothesis: Linked lifecycle history and explicit versioning provide a readable record and a route to the next cycle.
stages.caption: The activity history is filtered to the captured customer-journey scenario and shows its decision trail. The capture run verified a filtered JSON export. New-version creation is documented in the linked F06 flow, not separately executed in this screenshot run.
stages.limit: Local history is not immutable or shared audit infrastructure. Downloading the sample does not add an activity event.

recovery.title: Not ready to submit
recovery.when: Source, contracts or evidence still need work.
recovery.recovery: Save a named draft, then reopen Edit & submit draft. Incomplete drafts are allowed; submission still requires all required fields.

recovery.title: Reviewer asks for changes or rejects
recovery.when: A stage cannot approve the current submission.
recovery.recovery: Researcher reads the required reason and revises. Saving a revision draft preserves the reviewed state; explicit resubmission creates the next patch version and restarts all four stages.

recovery.title: Run fails or is cancelled
recovery.when: Use the seeded Failed run, or cancel an active demo run.
recovery.recovery: Open Run details, retry with the example mapping or restart. A local support request can be resolved by the Technical reviewer. Resolving support alone does not complete the run.

recovery.title: Output is not acceptable
recovery.when: Privacy reviewer rejects a specific artifact.
recovery.recovery: Download stays blocked. Read the reason, investigate and start a new run to produce a fresh output for review; there is no direct decision-overturn action.

recovery.title: The solo walkthrough is waiting
recovery.when: A review, publication, timer or output decision prevents continuing alone.
recovery.recovery: Use the quiet Simulation controls link. Simulate one/all reviews, separately simulate author publication, finish running demos or accept a pending output. Draft/revision submission rules still apply.

alternateEntry.title: Already have an approved method?
alternateEntry.text: Select or import a dataset, then start at Configure & run (J05) with an existing Approved pipeline. Its existing version does not repeat pipeline review for each run; the newly generated output still needs the separate Privacy decision. A new or revised method/version requires the full review path.
